hook_alternatives.copy: If you're backed up on a GLP-1 and eating less isn't helping, let me explain the gut slowdown nobody warned me about. Because once I understood it, everything changed.
My doctor put me on a GLP-1 and never once mentioned what it does to your gut. I had to find out from a Facebook group. Let me tell you what I learned.

I was two months into a GLP-1, dropping weight, and still waking up every morning feeling backed up and uncomfortable like nothing had moved. Let me tell you what I finally found out. Because nobody told me about it either.

cards.copy: If you're backed up on a GLP-1 and eating less isn't helping, let me explain the gut slowdown nobody warned me about. Because once I understood it, everything changed.
cards.visual: Presenter, chest-up in a lived-in kitchen; phone at eye level. She is already looking into the lens, ready to explain.
cards.performance: Direct, engaged; a small lean on let me explain. No greeting, bottle or opening logo.
cards.transition: Cold open into presenter; continue the same take into Because I was dropping weight.
cards.gap: Presenter identity, wardrobe and room need selection.

cards.copy: Because I was dropping weight. Like, the shot was actually working. But I felt backed up every single day, that uncomfortable fullness that just wouldn't shift no matter what I ate or didn't eat.
cards.visual: Stay on the same woman. One restrained hand gesture on the shot was actually working.
cards.performance: Confusion and mild frustration, conversational rather than alarmed.
cards.transition: Continue coverage; no mandatory cut at this beat boundary.
cards.gap: Same presenter take.

cards.copy: And that's the bit that messed with my head. My jeans were getting looser but I was still picking outfits around how my stomach felt. And I didn't really know how to explain that to anyone.
cards.visual: Optional short wardrobe insert: her hand hesitates between two tops; return to her for I did not really know how to explain that.
cards.performance: A brief private admission. No exaggerated shame performance.
cards.transition: Straight cut into insert on picking outfits; continuous voice; return on personal admission.
cards.gap: Unique wardrobe insert; same character/clothes continuity.

cards.copy: So let me tell you what I was actually missing because I genuinely thought losing the weight would fix it.
cards.visual: Presenter pauses, then returns attention to the lens. Maintain the same room and camera axis.
cards.performance: Let the renewed promise sound like she is remembering the explanation.
cards.transition: Stay on her through the next thought; a pickup cut only if the performance needs it.
cards.gap: Presenter coverage.

cards.copy: I was just scrolling through a GLP-1 support group on Facebook looking for answers and a gastroenterologist had left a comment on someone's post and it stopped me mid-scroll.
cards.visual: Optional over-shoulder phone scroll with generic text blocks; her thumb stops. No fabricated real Facebook post or named clinician.
cards.performance: Curious, recalling an ordinary scroll rather than announcing a breakthrough.
cards.transition: Insert at scrolling; return as she begins He said. Keep voice uninterrupted.
cards.gap: Original illustrative phone insert; any legible post needs a real source.

cards.copy: He said GLP-1 meds can slow down how fast your stomach empties. Like your stomach normally contracts to push food through, and when that slows down everything just backs up. Food, waste, gas. That's where the backed-up bloated feeling is actually coming from. It wasn't a weight thing at all. It was the gut slowdown.
cards.visual: Brief simple stomach-to-small-intestine educational view for empties/contracts, then return to her for the recognition. No rotting-food, universal obstruction or gas-explosion depiction.
cards.performance: Explain in her own voice, then land the personal realization.
cards.transition: Anatomy insert on how fast your stomach empties; straight return at It was not a weight thing.
cards.gap: Medical illustration and exact causal claims require review before generation.

cards.copy: And I thought okay, so that's why the fiber wasn't doing anything. Because fiber helps with regularity and MiraLAX moves water into the stool. Neither one actually touches the stomach emptying speed. I had completely missed that.
cards.visual: Distinct colon/stool-water illustration or neutral product-category props, followed by her reaction. Do not reuse the stomach view.
cards.performance: And I thought okay is a real reaction, not a sales pivot.
cards.transition: Insert only during the functional comparison; return at I had completely missed that.
cards.gap: Distinct illustration; no fake efficacy comparison graphics.

cards.copy: So I went back and DM'd him. I just asked what actually helps with the slowdown.
cards.visual: Keep her on camera; small glance down as she recalls sending the message.
cards.performance: A straightforward practical question.
cards.transition: Continue presenter; no second full phone-scroll scene.
cards.gap: Presenter coverage.

cards.copy: He wrote back. He said to look for ingredients that support gastric motility specifically. Something that helps the gut wall contract and actually move things through.
cards.visual: Same setup. She uses one small hand movement to explain move things through. No doctor avatar or white-coat cutaway.
cards.performance: Recount what she was told without switching into an expert voice.
cards.transition: Remain on her; brief pause before going back to the group.
cards.gap: Actual quoted authority/source remains a production dependency.

cards.copy: So I went back to the group and posted the question. And this woman who'd been on Ozempic for about eight months replied.
cards.visual: Same presenter; natural continuation of the story.
cards.performance: Keep this light and quick; no dramatic discovery cue.
cards.transition: Same take; no forced cut on So.
cards.gap: Presenter coverage.

cards.copy: She said she'd spent months researching this and found three specific ingredients that research showed actually addressed the gut slowdown directly. She walked me through each one.
cards.visual: She introduces the other woman’s explanation with a subtle three-finger gesture if natural.
cards.performance: Set up the list as useful advice, not an ingredient commercial.
cards.transition: Hold until First; no bottle or brand yet.
cards.gap: Source account and research claims require substantiation.

cards.copy: First was apigenin, which comes from celery juice. It's been shown in research to activate the receptors in the gut wall that trigger those contractions. The ones that actually move food forward.
cards.visual: Unbranded celery stalk/juice detail; small ingredient-name overlay apigenin. Return to her while she finishes the thought.
cards.performance: Slow slightly for the unfamiliar name, then return to ordinary speech.
cards.transition: Straight cut to ingredient on apigenin; no receptor activation animation.
cards.gap: Distinct celery asset; receptor/contraction claim remains unresolved.

cards.copy: Second was chlorophyllin, a plant compound. It's been studied clinically to bind the gas-producing stuff in the gut before it gets a chance to build pressure.
cards.visual: Separate chlorophyllin ingredient label beside a green ingredient sample on a neutral surface. Do not identify an ordinary leaf as the finished ingredient.
cards.performance: Matter-of-fact second job.
cards.transition: Cut on Second; return after the explanation. No disappearing-gas effect.
cards.gap: Correct ingredient form; clinical gas-binding claim remains unresolved.

cards.copy: Third was a soluble prebiotic fiber. But she was specific about it because the wrong type or too much can actually make the gas worse, not better.
cards.visual: Return to presenter for fiber. She gives a small cautionary hand gesture on the wrong type or too much.
cards.performance: Useful qualification, no alarm or condemnation of fiber.
cards.transition: Stay through the qualifier; no third repetitive ingredient macro required.
cards.gap: Presenter coverage; verify exact fiber/formula claim.

cards.copy: But she said she'd spent months trying to put it together herself first. Celery juice powder on its own. Chlorophyll supplements. Different fiber products. She tried all of it. None of it moved the needle the same way. She said the ratios have to be right and you can't just piece them together and get the same effect.
cards.visual: Optional overhead arrangement of three separate unbranded ingredient containers, then return to her while discussing the combination.
cards.performance: Tell it as someone else’s experiment she heard about.
cards.transition: Brief insert on putting it together herself; continuous narration.
cards.gap: Unique tabletop shot; do not depict a proven superiority experiment.

cards.copy: And the thing was, she'd looked. She couldn't find a single company that had put all three together properly. Until she found one.
cards.visual: Presenter, steady eye contact. Allow a short beat after Until she found one.
cards.performance: Understated anticipation, no exaggerated whisper.
cards.transition: Hold her face; product enters only after this line finishes.
cards.gap: Exclusivity claim requires support; preserve original copy in planning.

cards.copy: It was a gummy called Motilli.
cards.visual: She brings the approved current Motilli bottle into frame, label facing camera and readable.
cards.performance: Say the name simply, as the answer to her search.
cards.transition: Product entry on Motilli; no logo sting.
cards.gap: Approved bottle reference and physically plausible hand-held scale.

cards.copy: You take two before bed with a full glass of water which I honestly preferred because I'd already had enough capsules to last me a lifetime.
cards.visual: Unique close shot of exactly two correct gummies beside a full glass of water; return to her for the capsule preference.
cards.performance: The preference is personal relief, not a technical delivery claim.
cards.transition: Insert on two before bed; return on which I honestly preferred.
cards.gap: Current gummies and directions; product identity locked before generation.

cards.copy: And the first week, honestly, I saw no change. I nearly messaged her to say it wasn't working but I thought fine, I'll give it more time.
cards.visual: Presenter lowers the bottle out of frame; slight shrug or small half-smile.
cards.performance: Honest disappointment, without theatrical skepticism.
cards.transition: Natural pickup point; same room and identity.
cards.gap: Testimonial events need a factual basis before production.

cards.copy: Then around week two I had dinner with my husband and I got through the whole meal without thinking about my stomach once. Like I wasn't sitting there quietly uncomfortable the entire time waiting for it to pass. That sounds like nothing but I hadn't had that in months.
cards.visual: Optional warm dinner-table detail: relaxed hand, plate and companion’s hand at frame edge; return for That sounds like nothing.
cards.performance: The small ordinary improvement is the emotional center.
cards.transition: Insert on dinner; return before the understated meaning of the moment.
cards.gap: Unique dinner scene; do not generate purported customer proof.

cards.copy: By week three my mornings felt different. That heavy backed-up feeling when I woke up had started to ease. I wasn't laying there feeling like nothing had moved all night or rushing to the bathroom in a panic before I'd even had coffee.
cards.visual: Stay with her describing the morning. A light gesture toward herself is enough.
cards.performance: Relieved, reflective; no bathroom gag or staged pain performance.
cards.transition: Continuous coverage; no obligatory morning montage.
cards.gap: Testimonial timing/result dependency.

cards.copy: And the real test was just whether I could eat a normal amount and feel fine after. Not fine after I'd walked around the block and waited for it to settle. Just fine. Around the five or six week mark that was actually happening.
cards.visual: Stay on her face through Just fine. Allow a small pause before the later time point.
cards.performance: Conversational emphasis on the ordinary standard she wanted.
cards.transition: Hold instead of cutting away from the payoff.
cards.gap: Testimonial timing/result dependency.

cards.copy: So that was me two months ago. This is me now.
cards.visual: Remain on presenter. Genuine dated source footage may be inserted only if available. No synthetic flatter-stomach transformation.
cards.performance: A quiet statement of change.
cards.transition: Continue into the next sentence; no invented before/after card.
cards.gap: Genuine result imagery unavailable; presenter-only staging planned.

cards.copy: I get through dinner without planning to undo my jeans by dessert. That backed-up pressure that used to build from just a few bites has gone. I'm not mapping out my outfit in the morning around how uncomfortable I think I'm going to feel by lunchtime.
cards.visual: Presenter continues the dinner/clothes callbacks without replaying previous B-roll.
cards.performance: Warm, relieved and specific.
cards.transition: Sustained shot; no exact B-roll reuse.
cards.gap: Testimonial result dependency.

cards.copy: And I know the shot gets credit for the weight coming off. But the part that made me feel like myself again was getting rid of that constant uncomfortable feeling. Because you can be losing weight on a GLP-1 and still feel awful every single day. And nobody talks about that part. I'm sharing this because nobody told me either.
cards.visual: Presenter looks directly at the lens. Finish nobody told me either with empathy, not indignation.
cards.performance: This is the reason she is telling the story; let it breathe.
cards.transition: Same coverage into availability beat; no music crescendo prescribed.
cards.gap: Narrator’s role and account must be represented accurately.

cards.copy: The only thing she mentioned, and I've found this too, is they only do batches when the full formula is ready. So I've started ordering a spare bottle halfway through mine just so I'm not sitting around waiting on the next one.
cards.visual: Presenter with bottle resting naturally at frame edge. Avoid red stock counters or countdowns.
cards.performance: Practical detail, no urgency performance.
cards.transition: Optional clean pickup; no manufactured stock footage.
cards.gap: Batch/availability assertions need current support.

cards.copy: I'll drop the link below if you wanna have a look. Because if ninety days in it's not the difference you were hoping for, they give you a hundred percent of your money back. If that's you, the link's below.
cards.visual: Presenter invites the click with a small downward gesture; bottle remains visible. Final frame holds the product/CTA area.
cards.performance: Friendly, easy invitation, one destination.
cards.transition: Straight continuation into a 3-second final hold; no extra spoken copy.
cards.gap: Verify guarantee terms and destination before publication.
